subject: RE: RE: FW: the Feathers at five
body: A few of us are going to the Feathers at five. Your Monthly Status Report is also due tonight, and I am sure you have that in hand. No pressure either way. I will remember which you chose.

options.label: Go to the pub with your boss
Say that you have too much on

result.title: The Feathers
result.body: Your boss replies with a thumbs up. Later you can hear them all from the car park, and you are the only person left on the floor.

from: From: The Office Co-ordinator, Marjorie Tull
subject: ACTION REQUIRED: Speaking Up (mandatory, 45 minutes)
body: Our records show you have not completed the e-learning module Speaking Up. Any concerns about this module should be kept to yourself until you have completed it.

result.title: Speaking Up: completed
result.body: You score 100%. The certificate says that you feel safe to raise concerns. There is a box for concerns about the certificate, and it is not working.

options.label: Leave it running in another window

result.title: Speaking Up: completed
result.body: It finishes while you are at lunch. You score 100%.

reaction.believer: Your boss mentions, in passing, that the module takes forty-five minutes, and that the log says you did it in nine. Your boss does not ask anything further, and goes on not asking it for some time.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss mentions doing it the same way, and asks you how to make the window stay open.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss mentions doing it the same way, and that it would be a pity if the logs were ever read.

from: From: Office of the Chief Executive
subject: All-Colleague Town Hall: seats available
body: The Chief Executive will share the company's direction in person, on a large screen. Attendance is voluntary. Your attendance has been recorded.

options.label: Get there early and sit at the front

result.title: Town Hall recording
result.body: You watch it at twice the speed. The direction is the same, but more urgent.

subject: Slides for upstairs, by tomorrow
body: Your boss needs three slides for the floor above, by tomorrow. Your boss stresses that content is secondary at this stage, and that the last person's slides did not move.

options.label: Stay late and make everything fly in

result.title: Slides for upstairs
result.body: Each bullet point arrives from a different direction. The word Growth spins.

reaction.believer: Your boss watches it to the end, and asks which of the slides says what is happening. None of them does. Your boss asks you to try again, gently, which is worse.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss watches it twice, in silence, and asks whether you have ever thought about moving up.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss takes the file without comment. It goes upstairs that evening with a different name in the corner, and you are told that it went well.

options.label: Send three plain slides that say what is happening

result.title: Slides for upstairs
result.body: Three slides. Each of them says what is happening. It takes you twenty minutes.

reaction.believer: Your boss reads all three, then rings you to ask about the second. It is a real question. You have not been asked one here before.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss replies at 07:12 asking whether this is the draft.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss replies at 07:12: let's not put this in writing. The slides are not mentioned again, and neither, for a while, are you.

subject: Your Self-Assessment closes today
body: Please rate your own performance this year as Exceeds, Meets or Developing. There is no right answer. Developing is not available at your grade this year, because of the curve.

options.label: Spend an evening writing why you exceed

result.title: Self-Assessment submitted
result.body: You use the word impact eleven times. An automatic reply thanks you for your honesty, which it has rated Meets.

options.label: Tick Meets and close the window

result.title: Self-Assessment submitted
result.body: It takes four seconds. It is the most accurate thing you have written all year, and it will be read as a lack of ambition.

subject: Waiting on: figures from the Project Co-ordinator
body: Your report is due tonight, and it needs the figures from the Project Co-ordinator, which have not arrived. You have a read receipt, and an out-of-office that says back shortly. The report will go out with your name on it either way.

result.title: The figures
result.body: You stand beside the Project Co-ordinator's desk until the figures exist. You are thanked for your patience. You have lost most of an afternoon, and you still have a report to write.

options.label: Wait, and hope they come in time

result.title: The figures
result.body: They come in at 00:04, with an apology and the whole team copied in. The deadline was midnight. Someone upstairs, having nothing to go on, has coloured your project in for you.

result.title: The figures
result.body: They come in at 17:58, with no explanation and a small error, which you fix. You still have a report to write.

options.label: File it without them, and estimate

reaction.believer: Your boss asks where the figures in your report came from. You say that they are indicative. Your boss asks what they indicate.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss says that the report reads very confidently, and asks you to do them all like that.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss notes that the figures are estimates, and that they have your name on them, and files a copy.

result.title: Monthly Status Report filed
result.body: You file it at 23:58, marked amber, with the figures described as indicative. Nobody has ever asked what that means. Someone may.

subject: Monthly Status Report: due tonight
body: Your Monthly Status Report is due tonight, and nothing matters more to the people upstairs. Your project is really {real}. It was last reported as {reported}.

options.label: File it, and say how the project really is

result.title: Monthly Status Report filed
result.body: You file it at 23:58. An automatic reply confirms that your report has been received and may be read.

options.label: File it, and make the project green

reaction.believer: Your boss replies that this is good to hear, and asks what changed. You have no answer ready, and your boss waits for one.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss replies with three exclamation marks, and forwards it to everyone.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss replies with a single word: Noted. The report goes upstairs that night, and a copy goes into a drawer.

result.title: Monthly Status Report filed
result.body: You file it at 23:58. It is the greenest thing you have ever made. An automatic reply says that it may be read.

options.label: Do not file it, and see who notices

result.title: Monthly Status Report
result.body: You go home. By the morning someone upstairs, having nothing to go on, has coloured your project in for you, and not hopefully.
